title: The MacBook Air Is $200 Off During Prime Day, the Cheapest It’s Been Since June
gist: The M5 MacBook Air is $200 off at $1,099 on Amazon, effectively reversing Apple's June 2026 $200 price increase, but still well above early-2026 sub-$1,000 street prices and the $749 Prime Day 2025 price; the reviewer warns MacBook Pro buyers to wait for a rumored OLED touchscreen model.

themes.theme: Apple's 2026 price hike and laptop inflation

insights.claim: Apple raised MacBook prices by $200 in June 2026, and the $200 Prime Day discount on the M5 MacBook Air ($1,299 to $1,099) effectively just undoes that increase.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Headline 'deals' in 2026 are largely restoring pre-hike prices, not true markdowns — consumer electronics pricing has reset upward.
insights.quote: This sale effectively undoes that increase, which is heartening in a time of seemingly endless price hikes across the tech industry.
insights.locator: This is the best price I've seen

insights.claim: The MacBook Air frequently dipped below $1,000 in the first half of 2026 and sold for $749 on Prime Day 2025, so even the discounted $1,099 price is sharply higher year over year.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: A ~47% YoY rise in the best-available deal price for the flagship laptop signals material hardware cost inflation flowing to consumers.
insights.quote: You could have bought it for $749 during Prime Day in 2025.
insights.locator: Of course, that's still more expensive

insights.claim: The reviewer expects pre-hike MacBook Air prices are not returning soon, framing the higher price level as structural rather than temporary.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Implies sustained elevated ASPs for Apple Macs and a tougher volume backdrop for PC demand.
insights.quote: But those prices aren't coming back anytime soon
insights.locator: Of course, that's still more expensive

insights.claim: The baseline $1,099 deal configuration ships with 16 GB RAM and 512 GB storage, with the same $200 cut applied to higher configurations including the 15-inch model.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Uniform dollar discounts across SKUs point to a retailer/Apple program rather than inventory clearing of specific configs.
insights.locator: A number of MacBooks are on sale

insights.claim: The MacBook Neo's '$10 off' is not a real sale, since it has sat at that price for many months.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Persistent token discounts on the entry Mac suggest limited promotional room on the low-end product.
insights.quote: The MacBook Neo is “on sale” for $10 off, though it's been at that price for many months.
insights.locator: I wouldn't buy the other MacBooks

insights.claim: Reports point to an updated OLED MacBook Pro possibly arriving as soon as October 2026 that would bring a proper touchscreen to the Mac for the first time, so the reviewer advises waiting rather than buying the current, post-hike MacBook Pro.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: A touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro would be a major Mac form-factor shift and a catalyst for a pro-upgrade cycle (and OLED panel suppliers).
insights.quote: This is the anticipated OLED model that has been in the works for years, which would introduce a proper touchscreen to the Mac for the first time.
insights.locator: The MacBook Pro isn't on a noteworthy sale
